name: Broken Tools
summary: At the dig northwest of Bloodhoof Village, dwarven picks lie broken at the forge. Baine Bloodhoof seeks proof that the excavation threatening Mulgore's land and wildlife has stopped.

sections.title: Sabotaging the Dig
sections.body: Northwest of Bloodhoof Village, dwarven excavators search Mulgore's hills for traces of ancient history. The tauren see the digging as a defilement of the Earth Mother. Its noise and destruction unsettle the local wildlife, especially the roaming kodo herds. So young Baine Bloodhoof orders defenders to take the prospectors' iron picks and break them at a forge. With the picks ruined, the expedition cannot gouge farther into the earth.

faq.answer: Broken Tools are ruined Prospector's Picks taken from the dwarven excavators in Mulgore and crushed at a forge. Their heads are ruined and their shafts splintered.

faq.q: Why does Baine Bloodhoof want them destroyed?
faq.answer: Baine believes digging into the soil defiles the land and angers Mulgore's wildlife, especially the kodos. Breaking the picks stops the excavation and warns the dwarves that reckless digging will not reveal the land's wisdom.

faq.q: Where can these picks be broken?
faq.answer: You can break the picks at any working forge. One stands at the dwarven dig site, and others can be found in Bloodhoof Village or Thunder Bluff.

faq.q: Why are dwarves digging in Mulgore?
faq.answer: The dwarves believe Mulgore's soil holds deep secrets and relics of antiquity. They search for their origins by hollowing out foreign lands, heedless of the people who live there.

angles.text: As a tauren, bringing ruined tools to Baine helps defend the Earth Mother from digging that torments the native beasts.
As a blacksmith, you can turn your forge and anvil against dwarven ironwork to defend the land.
